title: U.S. House · Kentucky's 2nd District
area: South-central Kentucky, including Bowling Green, Owensboro and Elizabethtown.

candidates.name: Brett Guthrie
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative, Kentucky's 2nd District (since 2009); Chair, House Committee on Energy and Commerce

priorities.text: Technology: focused on improving cellular and broadband service in rural areas and "maintaining America's technological competitive edge against the Chinese Communist Party."
Health Care: as Chair of the Energy and Commerce Committee's Health Subcommittee, says he advances policies to lower costs through competition and price transparency.
Fiscal Responsibility: says he wants to get the national debt under control and has consistently supported a balanced budget amendment to the Constitution.

positions.summary: Says climate change is a real and serious threat but does not support the Green New Deal, favoring an "all-of-the-above" energy strategy and market-based solutions.
positions.quote: I am a member of the Conservative Climate Caucus and think that climate change is a real and serious threat. However, I do not believe that radical solutions proposed in the Democrats’ “Green New Deal” are the solution. The Green New Deal is projected to cost up to $93 trillion over ten years, at an estimated cost of over $60,000 per year per household. I believe that we need innovative and market-based solutions to combat climate change.

positions.summary: Calls Democratic proposals for government-run health care financially "disastrous," grouping it with other policies he opposes as reckless spending.
positions.quote: The Democrats’ proposed policies such as the Green New Deal, government-run health care, and other reckless spending packages would be disastrous for the financial stability of our country.

positions.summary: Said he voted for S. 2, the Secure America Act, which funds ICE and CBP enforcement operations through fiscal year 2029, and criticized “catch-and-release policies.”
positions.quote: Our nation cannot afford to return to the open borders and catch-and-release policies that caused the worst immigration crisis in our nation’s history. I was proud to vote in favor of legislation to provide funding for essential border security and immigration enforcement operations through September 2029,

record.text: Chairs the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (119th Congress, 2025-2026).
Chaired the Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Health in the 118th Congress (2023-2024) before becoming full committee chair.

candidates.name: Megan Wingfield
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary with 40.7% of the vote, defeating Hank Linderman, David Hatfield and William Compton.

priorities.text: Campaigns on affordable healthcare and support for working families.

positions.summary: Platform page lists Medicare for All among her stated healthcare positions and calls for universal, affordable, accessible healthcare.
positions.quote: Expanding affordable housing programs and supporting Medicare for All to ease financial burdens.

positions.summary: Platform page says she would protect reproductive freedom and the right to choose.
positions.quote: Protect reproductive freedom and the right to choose.

positions.summary: Platform page says she is pushing for tax equity in which corporations and the ultra-wealthy pay their fair share.
positions.quote: Pushing for tax equity—where corporations and the ultra-wealthy pay their fair share.

positions.summary: Platform page lists raising the minimum wage among her economic commitments.
positions.quote: Raising the minimum wage and protecting gig workers and union organizing efforts.

candidates.name: Thomas Loecken

priorities.text: In a 2018 Advocate-Messenger questionnaire: "I will work to roll back changes that have been made to our clean air, water and land acts."
In a 2018 Advocate-Messenger questionnaire: "I believe the role of a representative is to see that the needs of their constituents are met, whether it’s healthcare, tax reform, jobs, infrastructure"

positions.summary: In a 2018 newspaper questionnaire, named raising the minimum wage as his example of an unmet need in the district.
positions.quote: to pick one, lets go with raising the minimum wage.

statements.quote: Global Warming. It’s here and it’s man-made. If you value the world you will leave to your children then this needs to be addressed.
statements.context: In a 2018 Advocate-Messenger candidate questionnaire (his 2018 campaign for this seat)
